title: The 7 Deadly Sins of Prompting: briefs, not wishes, and the R-E-X prompt
summary: Ruben argues most ChatGPT prompts fail because they are wishes rather than briefs. He lists seven common prompting mistakes with before/after fixes and offers the R-E-X framework (Role, Examples, Expectations). Iterating in short steps beats writing one long prompt.

principles.text: Prompts fail when they are wishes. Write a brief: good inputs produce good outputs.
principles.quote: Most (ChatGPT) prompts fail because they’re wishes, not briefs.

principles.text: Give the model context: role, task scope and constraints. Otherwise it guesses and errors multiply.
principles.quote: the model guesses your job, audience, and constraints. Guessing multiplies errors.

principles.text: Turn questions into jobs with deliverables; define success and acceptance tests up front.
principles.quote: Asking questions is level 1. Give it directives.

principles.text: Split big asks into steps and chain outputs, instead of one giant request.
principles.quote: One giant ask hides failures and creates spaghetti outputs.

principles.text: Iteration beats length: prompt quicker, not longer. It's a chat, so have a chat with it.
principles.quote: Iteration beats length: prompt quicker, not longer.

principles.text: Use R-E-X: define a Role, paste Examples to imitate, and set Expectations (format, length, tone, rubric).
principles.quote: The R-E-X prompt is to define a role, give examples & set expectations in your (ChatGPT, or other AI) prompt.
